blocks.content: 3. terraform force-unlock
terraform force-unlock is the real command that genuinely releases a stuck lock, used deliberately, and genuinely carefully, not as a casual, everyday first response.
This command takes the real, exact lock ID from the error message, explicitly, deliberately confirming exactly which lock is genuinely being released.
This is worth treating as a real, deliberate, last-resort action, only after genuinely confirming the situation actually warrants it.

4. Real, Common Causes
A crashed CI job, or a genuinely killed local process, mid-apply, are the real, most common causes of a stuck, real lock actually needing this treatment.
In both real, common cases, the operation that originally acquired the lock never genuinely got the chance to release it cleanly, afterward.
Recognizing these real, common patterns helps confirm, honestly, that a genuine, stuck lock, rather than an actually still-running operation, is the real cause.
This connects directly to the real, honest verification step covered next, before ever actually force-unlocking anything.

5. Verify Before Force-Unlocking
Before genuinely force-unlocking, confirm no real operation is actually, still genuinely running, checking with a real team member, or the CI system directly.
Force-unlocking a lock that is genuinely still, actively in use can cause real, genuine, and considerably worse state corruption than the original conflict.
This real, honest verification step is worth treating as absolutely non-negotiable, every single time, before running force-unlock at all.
This connects directly back to the real, careful, deliberate discipline already emphasized consistently throughout this entire course.

blocks.content: 6. The Real Lock ID
The real lock ID, displayed directly in the genuine error message, is exactly what force-unlock actually needs, copied precisely, not approximated.
This real, exact ID confirms deliberately that the correct, specific, genuine lock is actually the one being released, not some other, unrelated one.
This small, real, practical detail is worth double-checking directly, a mistyped ID simply fails, rather than genuinely releasing the wrong lock.
This connects directly back to the real error message already covered, worth reading carefully enough to copy this ID correctly.

blocks.content: 7. A Real, Complete Example
Bringing this topic together, a real, complete resolution reads the error, confirms no genuine operation is still running, and then force-unlocks deliberately.
This is worth treating as a genuine, real, step-by-step template for the next time this exact, real situation genuinely arises.
Every practice covered in this topic individually comes together here, into one, coherent, real, safe resolution process.
This real sequence, read, verify, then act, is worth applying consistently to every troubleshooting topic covered throughout this entire module.

# 1. Read the real error, note the lock ID
# 2. Confirm with the team: is anyone genuinely still applying?
# 3. If genuinely confirmed stuck:
terraform force-unlock a1b2c3d4-...

blocks.text: 9. When force-unlock Genuinely Is Not Enough

blocks.content: If the underlying, real state itself was genuinely, partially written before the crash, force-unlocking alone may not genuinely fix everything, worth inspecting state afterward.
A quick terraform plan, immediately after unlocking, reveals whether real, genuine state corruption actually occurred, or the state remains genuinely intact.
